summary: Two local assertions disproved analytically; corresponding conditional/local repairs support the inspected main uses. No refutation of Theorem 2.4 established.

source_location.claim: Theorem 2.3(iii), especially membership asserted for every p in [1,infinity] under u0 in Lq, q in (1,2).

assumption_checks: Nonnegative finite Radon density with mass one.
K(u0) tangential with magnitude 1/(2*pi) for r<1 and 1/(2*pi*r) for r>=1; in weak L2.
Distributional divergence zero, curl u0; no circulation atom at origin.
Radial heat evolution has zero nonlinear advection, is smooth for t>0 and is a vorticity solution obtained by radial regularization.
counterexample.exact_result: u(t,0)=erf(1/(2*sqrt(t)))/(4*sqrt(pi*t)) tends to infinity as t decreases to zero.

problems.check_type: complete analytic counterexample, with optional numerical illustration
problems.counterevidence: The proof on page 10 explicitly assumes u0 in Lp. Interpreting that as a missing hypothesis yields a valid conditional propagation result.
problems.core_dependency: Applications on pp.23 and 25 already impose L4 initial data and have L1 mass. The corrected condition suffices in the inspected applications.
problems.impact: Auxiliary theorem range is overstated; no demonstrated loss of central uniqueness or its checked L4 uses.

repair.statement: For each p, add u0 in Lp to the original Lq assumption before asserting uniform Lp propagation.
repair.verified_scope: Jensen/mass-one kernel argument gives the claimed propagation under the added condition.

source_location.claim: Appendix proof of Lemma .1, display after (0.19): convergence of gradient resolvent applied to compactly supported smooth phi in global L1.

counterexample.input: Normalized nonnegative radial smooth bump C*exp(-1/(1-r^2)) for r<1, zero otherwise.
assumption_checks: C positive finite normalizing constant, phi in C_c^infinity(R2), mass one.
For r>1, K(phi)=x_perp/(2*pi*r^2), so its global L1 norm diverges.
Each fixed positive resolvent parameter has L1 gradient kernel: integral exp(-epsilon*t)*C*t^(-1/2) dt is finite.
counterexample.exact_result: Each approximant is in L1, but its proposed limit and even their difference are not in L1.

problems.check_type: complete analytic counterexample and repaired argument
problems.counterevidence: (0.17)-(0.18) provide local domination, proving L1_loc and distributional convergence; no OCR ambiguity after image inspection.
problems.core_dependency: Lemma .1 supports (3.20), then the energy proof of Theorem 2.4. The needed distributional identity and multiplier estimate remain valid; global L1 convergence is unnecessary.
problems.impact: False stronger auxiliary topology, with no demonstrated loss of required central estimate.

repair.statement: Replace global L1 convergence by L1_loc convergence, hence distributional convergence.
repair.verified_scope: Local dominated convergence, compact convolution, distributional resolvent identity and L4/3-to-L4 density extension; independent Fourier bound validates (3.20).

limitations: Publisher version not acquired or compared.
External elliptic and probabilistic cited theorems not independently reproved.
The full pathwise uniqueness class in Theorem 4.5 and full mass-conservation justification of Corollary 3.1 not certified.
No author code run and no full empirical reproduction.

problems_checked.P1: Independently rederived radial mass-one density u0=1/(2*pi*r)1_(0,1), its L^(4/3) membership and divergence-free weak-L2 Biot-Savart velocity; Theorem2.1 p7 has no missing smallness assumption violated by this atom-free density. Radial heat evolution solves the nonlinear vorticity equation because tangential velocity has zero radial advection. Polar integration gives u(t,0)=erf(1/(2*sqrt(t)))/(4*sqrt(pi*t)), unbounded as t->0. Thus the separately stated all-p uniform membership at p9 is false. The p10 proof explicitly adds initial Lp; doubly mass-one kernel Jensen gives the valid conditional bound. The p25 L4 probability-density application already has required L4 (and interpolated L4/3), so this is a range overstatement without demonstrated damage to that central use: retain Minor. No theorem2.4 counterexample claimed.
problems_checked.P2: Independently checked the mass-one radial C_c^infinity bump. Its K field equals x_perp/(2*pi*r^2) outside support, so integral of its magnitude is infinite. Each positive-parameter resolvent gradient is L1 from integral e^(-epsilon*t)t^(-1/2)dt. Therefore even the difference is not global L1. Actual source p26 states global L1. On compact sets |k|=1/(2*pi*r) is integrable, giving L1_loc and D' convergence after compact convolution; the Fourier multiplier resolvent identity and bound |xi|^2/(epsilon+|xi|^2)<=1 retain the needed (3.20) estimate. Stronger global topology is unnecessary, so retain Minor with exact corrected topology.
